core_obligations: Use the base change statement to reduce to the case where A is local with maximal ideal p (proof lines 28036-28037).
Use the well-definedness statement to replace M^bullet by a quasi-isomorphic complex (proof lines 28037-28038).

Use freeness of the cohomology modules to conclude that M^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to the complex with term H^i(M^bullet) in degree i and vanishing differentials, quoting the Derived Categories statement (proof lines 28039-28043).
Conclude that one may assume all differentials in M^bullet are zero (proof lines 28044-28045).
With vanishing differentials, observe that I_i(M^bullet, f) = (f^{r_i}) is principal, completing the proof (proof lines 28045-28046).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, a prime p, a nonzerodivisor f, and a bounded complex M^bullet of finite free A-modules, and assumes that H^i(M^bullet)_p is free for all i; it concludes that I_i(M^bullet, f)_p is a principal ideal, in fact generated by a power of f, for all i (source lines 28026-28033). The proof reduces along two axes. First, by the base change statement one may assume A is local with maximal ideal p (proof lines 28036-28037). Second, by the well-definedness statement one may replace M^bullet by a quasi-isomorphic complex (proof lines 28037-28038). The key step uses the freeness hypothesis: by the freeness of the cohomology modules, M^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to the complex whose term in degree i is H^i(M^bullet) with vanishing differentials, quoting the Derived Categories statement (proof lines 28039-28043). In other words one may assume all differentials in M^bullet vanish (proof lines 28044-28045). With vanishing differentials it is clear that I_i(M^bullet, f) = (f^{r_i}) is principal, completing the proof (proof lines 28045-28046). The non-routine content is the recognition that free cohomology over a local ring splits the complex into its cohomology modules, after which the invariants are visibly principal.
